reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BC Trader as an exclusive cryptocurrency trading platform, soliciting a $500 bot license and a further $2,000 trading-fund requirement while asking users to connect an exchange API key and presenting profit-related performance claims. Although the speakers acknowledge possible losses and variable results, the video frames this combination as a financially risky promotional scheme, without establishing purchases, deposits, API permissions, or completed losses.

This is not for anybody else, this is only for bit club network.

So just understand this thing really works, it is tested, it is proven

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise uniform or guaranteed returns; it expressly warns that misuse could cost users money, acknowledges that some people may receive poor gains, and shows that the test account was losing 1%. It also tells viewers not to buy the bot unless they have separate trading funds. Those qualifications are inconsistent with a deceptive assurance of risk-free profit. The discussion presents uncertainty, user discretion, and the possibility of loss as central parts of the decision, so the evidence supports a candid risk-warning presentation rather than a scam claim.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the price, funding requirement, and profit language, but those points omit the surrounding qualifications. The speaker does not describe a guaranteed outcome; instead, the webinar expressly discusses poor gains, losses, and the need for additional trading capital. A paid license and a risk warning can coexist without establishing deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: there will be people that will not get very good gains.
that's actually losing 1%.
I wouldn't even... To be honest with you if you had $500 to trade... that's even kind of pushing it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk disclosures do not erase the promotional core. The same presentation tells viewers to ensure buyers in their downline watch the webinar, recommends purchasing a $500 license with $2,000 in the trading account, and says the system is tested and proven. Mentioning possible losses can make a solicitation sound balanced without showing that the underlying claims are reliable.

opening.argument: The recording is structured as a practical webinar explaining how the software works: the presenters discuss algorithms, exchange connections, portfolio views, trading limits, maintenance, API behavior, and how users can interpret results. The screen share shows onboarding instructions, algorithm listings, market data, and portfolio information rather than a completed customer transaction or demonstrated payout. The speakers repeatedly frame the session as instruction, including telling viewers that questions will be covered and that the webinar will explain the system. On this evidence, the central activity is technology education and operational demonstration.

citations.quote: We're going to be covering absolutely everything.
we did not know some things we guess and we thought we understood and then tonight you're gonna learn we were completely wrong
sometimes API keys won't pick up some balances

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a webinar does not change what the webinar is about. The instructional format is used to explain how to purchase access, connect an exchange, fund an account, and select algorithms. A demonstration can still be promotional when the subject is a paid trading product and the audience is directed toward using it.

citations.quote: if you have anybody that buys the bader, in your downline, you need to make sure the very first thing they do is watch this webinar.
if you're gonna buy the $500 license, you need to have $2000 to put in that trading account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational detail is not neutral. The webinar is expressly for a platform available only through the network, tells viewers how much capital to pair with the license, and discusses expected profitability. Showing an interface and explaining its controls therefore supports product promotion, not merely technology education.

citations.quote: This is not for anybody else, this is only for bit club network.
I think you will make a profit after one year

opening.argument: At most, the evidence shows promotion of an ordinary software service with a paid license and optional trading activity. The record does not establish that anyone purchased access, deposited funds, granted harmful permissions, suffered a loss, or received a guaranteed return. The interface depicts algorithms, exchange labels, market values, and portfolio holdings, while the discussion explains usage limits and maintenance. Even the API material concerns connecting an exchange account and troubleshooting incomplete data, not a request for passwords or a demonstrated theft mechanism. Without a shown scam mechanism or completed harm, the safer classification is ordinary commerce.

citations.quote: just looking back at the actual data
this account doesn't have zero in it but you'll see the graph suddenly dropped to zero
if something's going down and the other one's not going down it's going to be you know putting it over on the other one

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution does not need a completed victim transaction to identify risky promotion, but it also cannot treat ordinary commerce as evidence of a scam. The supplied material shows a software product, a license, exchange integration, and variable trading results; it does not show a completed purchase, deposit, credential disclosure, or loss. The absence of those mechanisms matters when distinguishing promotion from demonstrated fraud.

citations.quote: this account doesn't have zero in it
just looking back at the actual data

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing completed loss is not exculpatory because the content itself solicits participation. It promotes an exclusive platform, directs buyers in a downline to watch, requires a paid license plus trading capital, and presents profit-related claims. The interface and maintenance notices show a functioning product, but they do not validate the commercial claims or remove the financial solicitation.
